ev.q: From 2010 to 2011, the number of birth defects surveillance programs involved in CCHD screening increased from one to 10.
Sixty-seven percent of programs reported that it took ≥12 months to complete birth defects surveillance case records.
CCHD activities increased from one state in 2010 to 10 states in 2011
Sixty-eight percent of programs did not have access to hospital point-of-care screening records.
CCHD activities increased from one state in 2010 to 10 states in 2011
CDC partnered with the National Birth Defects Prevention Network (NBDPN) to conduct a survey
States were surveyed in November 2010, after the initial SACHDNC recommendation, and again in November 2011

methods_quotes.q: The 2010 and 2011 surveys were completed in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, and Puerto Rico, for a response rate of 100%.
The 2010 and 2011 surveys were distributed to the same person in each program
Nonresponders were contacted via e-mail and telephone.
